title: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Vaping enforcement response launch
sections.summary: Sitting suspended until 3.30 pm; on 1 September 2025 the Government launched a coordinated response to enhance vaping enforcement due to etomidate-laced vaporisers or Kpods.

sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 3.04 pm until 3.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On 1 September 2025, the Government launched a coordinated response to enhance the enforcement approach towards vaping, due to the emergence of etomidate-laced vaporisers or "Kpods".

sections.label: Vaporiser offence arrests figures
sections.summary: Over the past six months, more than 5,100 persons were caught for vaporiser-related offences, of whom 593 are etomidate vaporiser users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Over the past six months, we have caught more than 5,100 persons for vaporiser-related offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Of these, more than one in 10, or 593, are etomidate vaporiser users.

sections.label: New law on vaporisers
sections.summary: A new law will prohibit vaporisers and allow enforcement against abuse of etomidate and potentially other psychoactive substances through such delivery devices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These past six months have been critical, not just for enforcement, but also to consolidate lessons from our enforcement experience and review our laws.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We are now ready to put in place a new law, which will not only prohibit vaporisers, but will also allow for enforcement against the abuse of etomidate and potentially other psychoactive substances through such delivery devices in the future.

sections.label: TVCA, SPS and controlled drugs
sections.summary: The TVCA will focus on SPS while the MDA continues to govern controlled drugs, so controlled drugs are not included in the TVCA Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The TVCA will focus on SPS, while the MDA will continue to govern the abuse of controlled drugs, including those abused through vaporisers or tobacco products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, controlled drugs will not be included in this Schedule under the TVCA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: One, a rebuttable presumption that such substances have a psychoactive effect when consumed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Two, for prosecution purposes, a person is deemed to have the knowledge that a product or substance is an SPS as long as the person knows that the SPS has a psychoactive effect when consumed.

sections.label: Stiffer penalties for SPS products
sections.summary: Stiffer penalties will apply to offences related to prohibited products, tobacco products, vaporisers and imitation tobacco products containing SPS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Stiffer penalties will be applied to offences related to the products I just described – prohibited products, as well as tobacco products, vaporisers and imitation tobacco products containing SPS, that is, SPS products.

sections.label: Penalties for SPS offences
sections.summary: Supplying SPS products carries two to 10 years imprisonment and two to five strokes of the cane, with stiffer penalties for importers and fines or imprisonment for possession, purchase or consumption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As Members can see on the handouts, individuals who supply SPS products will face two to 10 years imprisonment term and two to five strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Those who import these products will face stiffer penalties – three to 20 years imprisonment term and five to 15 strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And those caught possessing or purchasing such products, or consuming SPS, if prosecuted, can be liable to a fine of up to $20,000, or imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both.

sections.label: Increased fine for purchase possession
sections.summary: The maximum fine for purchase, use and possession is increased from $2,000 to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For purchase, use and possession, the maximum fine will be increased from $2,000 to $10,000.

sections.label: Presumption for vaporisers in vehicles
sections.summary: Under new section 16C, a driver with vaporisers found in a vehicle entering Singapore is presumed to possess them and cannot claim ignorance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, with the new presumption under section 16C, if vaporisers are found in a vehicle entering Singapore, the driver of that vehicle will be presumed to be in possession of the vaporisers, and cannot avoid legal liability by simply claiming ignorance that the vaporisers are present in the vehicle.

sections.label: Warehouse seizure and storage offence
sections.summary: A warehouse seizure exceeded 400,000 vaporisers and components worth over $5 million, and new section 18A makes it an offence for owners and occupiers to allow storage of prohibited products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The largest warehouse seizure exceeded 400,000 vaporisers and components, worth more than $5 million in street value.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under the new section 18A, introduced by clause 10, it is an offence for owners and occupiers of land, buildings and places to allow other individuals to store prohibited products in these spaces.

sections.label: Powers to seize vehicles and cash
sections.summary: New powers allow seizure of vehicles and trailers reasonably suspected of use in TVCA offences, and cash reasonably suspected as evidence of a TVCA offence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To facilitate enforcement, particularly against importers and suppliers of prohibited products, we are also introducing new powers to seize vehicles and trailers reasonably suspected of being used, or is intended to be used in connection with committing an offence under the TVCA, and to seize cash that is reasonably suspected to be evidence that a TVCA offence has been committed.

sections.label: New SPS product category penalties
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new category of products containing SPS, with penalties aligned to the MDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new category of products containing SPS, with penalties aligned to the MDA.

sections.label: Community orders and DRC escalation
sections.summary: Community-based orders are introduced for rehabilitation, with escalation to institutional treatment in DRCs for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On rehabilitation, community-based orders are introduced, with escalation to institutional treatment in DRCs for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Vaporiser possession penalties increased
sections.summary: Penalties for possessing and using vaporisers rise significantly, with fines of up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Penalties for possession and use of vaporisers increase significantly, with fines up to $10,000.

sections.label: Etomidate MDA listing delisting
sections.summary: Etomidate and its analogues will be listed and delisted from the MDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Etomidate and its analogues will be listed and delisted from the MDA.

sections.label: Youth protection enforcement rehabilitation questions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether youths are protected, residents see enforcement, and scheduling stays ahead of evolving substances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, are we protecting youths with measurable outcomes, fair safeguards and properly resourced rehabilitation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, will residents see visible enforcement, accountable powers and clarity on the ground?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, are we staying ahead of evolving substances through rapid scheduling, predictive monitoring and upstream disruption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we answer these well, this Bill will not merely add penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will reduce exposure, restore confidence and protect families.

sections.label: Heavy penalties for vape sellers
sections.summary: The speaker supports fines up to $200,000 and six years' jail for vape sellers who profit from the trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On the other hand, we must clamp down heavily on those who profit off the vape trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, different penalty regimes and the move to impose a fine of up to $200,000 and six years' jail for vape sellers is one which I support wholeheartedly.

sections.label: Tobacco excise duty increase
sections.summary: Tobacco excise duties rose 20% to 58.9 cents per cigarette, with FY2025 duties expected to increase over $92.9 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, this Bill's Second Reading comes at the heels of this year's Budget, where it was announced that tobacco excise duties were increased by 20% from 49.1 cents to 58.9 cents per cigarette.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For financial year (FY) 2025, tobacco duties are expected to increase by over $92.9 million, compared to financial year 2023 when tobacco duties were last increased.

sections.label: Smoking disease burden survey
sections.summary: The Global Burden of Disease survey states about 66,000 disability-adjusted life years are lost yearly to smoking.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the Global Burden of Disease survey, some 66,000 disability-adjusted life years are lost per annum to smoking.

sections.label: Smoking cohort ban proposal
sections.summary: Speaker cites other countries' bans and Singapore's 8.4% smoking rate, urging a smoking cohort ban and cessation targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Although New Zealand may have made a U-turn, other countries such as the Maldives have also implemented a similar ban, with the United Kingdom (UK) seeking to implement a similar measure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our smoking rate has dropped to an all-time low of 8.4%, in no small part due to the efforts of the Government and society at large.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, if the authorities have the wherewithal to impose bans on chewable tobacco and vapes as well as leave the door open to a ban on flavoured tobacco products, I am confident that we can also move decisively to impose a smoking cohort ban, as I have previously mentioned during my Committee of Supply cut for MOH.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also hope that we can set out targets for complete smoking cessation over time as an end game that we can all work towards.

sections.label: Bill's prevention and rehabilitation direction
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes the Bill for strengthening prevention, tightening controls and providing community-centred early intervention and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the direction of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It strengthens prevention upstream, it tightens controls where harm begins and it also provides a framework for early intervention and importantly, rehabilitation that is centred in the community, where I think that is the safer and wiser approach.

sections.label: Community-based rehabilitation orders
sections.summary: Speaker says rehabilitative pathways, including community-based rehabilitation orders, are an important and integral part of the amendment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: They want and look for a way back.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: So, the inclusion of rehabilitative pathways, including community-based rehabilitation orders, is a very important and integral part of this amendment.

sections.label: Duties on responsible persons
sections.summary: Speaker says the Bill places duties on responsible persons of specified premises for access controls, age checks and reporting obligations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In Parliament, we can discuss and debate clauses, but on the ground, it comes down to people, processes and clarity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill places duties on responsible persons of specified premises in relation to access controls, age checks and reporting obligations.

sections.label: Calibrated response to vaping challenge
sections.summary: Speaker says clear rules, fair processes and supported officers improve enforcement, calling the Bill a careful response to vaping and smoking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If rules are clear, processes are fair and officers are supported, enforcement would become more consistent and confidence in the system would increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill represents a careful and calibrated response to the growing public health challenge of vapes and smoking substances.

sections.label: Tobacco deaths and disability study
sections.summary: Speaker cites a 2023 Global Burden of Disease study reporting 2,043 tobacco deaths and 660,152 disability adjusted life years in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a Global Burden of Disease study in 2023, Singapore saw 2,043 deaths from tobacco and 660,152 disability adjusted life years, which are the years of life lost and years lived in disability.

sections.label: Cohort tobacco ban proposal
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a cohort tobacco ban so younger generations never start smoking, noting the Government is open to studying it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond residential smoking issues, we must move beyond managing the prevalence of smoking and start legislating for its eventual elimination for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I reiterate my call from 5 March 2024 and echo my hon friend, Ms He Ting Ru, regarding a cohort tobacco ban.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will ensure that younger generations of Singaporeans never start smoking, creating a smoke-free future for our children and our children's children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I was glad to hear Minister of State Rahayu Mahzam say during the Committee of Supply debate on 5 March 2026 that the Government remains open to a cohort smoking ban and will study its effectiveness and how it can be applied to Singapore's context.

sections.label: Cap on nicotine yield
sections.summary: The Minister is urged to use clause 6 powers to cap nicotine yield in tobacco smoke, citing the EU and UK 1.0 milligram limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to exercise the powers granted under clause 6 of the Bill to set a stringent cap on the nicotine yield in the smoke of all tobacco products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that in the European Union and the UK, the maximum emission level is strictly limited, and the nicotine yield cannot exceed 1.0 milligrams per cigarette.

sections.label: Nicotine analogues and psychoactive substances
sections.summary: Expanded definitions for nicotine analogues and a Specified Psychoactive Substances framework let enforcement respond swiftly as substances evolve.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The expansion of definitions to capture nicotine analogues and the creation of a Specified Psychoactive Substances framework ensure that enforcement can respond swiftly as substances evolve.

sections.label: Penalties and duties for import supply
sections.summary: Stronger import and supply penalties, presumptions against denying knowledge, and owner and occupier duties set a clear hierarchy of culpability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The strengthened penalties for import and supply, the presumptions preventing easy denial of knowledge and the duties placed on owners and occupiers to prevent storage and distribution draw a clear hierarchy of culpability.

sections.label: Rehabilitation orders for nicotine exposure
sections.summary: Because nicotine and psychoactive substances affect adolescent impulse control and judgement, the speaker welcomes structured rehabilitation orders with community and family involvement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Nicotine and psychoactive substance exposure affect impulse control and judgement, particularly in adolescents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the structured rehabilitation orders introduced in this Bill, including community-based rehabilitation and family involvement.

sections.label: Vape detection in IHL campuses
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there are plans to install vape detection systems in the porous campuses and hostels of institutes of higher learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My last question: the campus and the hostels of the institutes of higher learning (IHLs) are really porous and do we have plans to install vapes detection systems in the IHL campus and hostels?

sections.label: Etomidate misuse in vaporisers
sections.summary: Etomidate and its analogues, developed as medical anaesthetics, are being misused in vaporisers, exploiting regulatory gaps between existing frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Specifically, we are seeing the rise of substances, like etomidate, and its analogues, originally developed as medical anaesthetics, which are being misused in vaporisers in ways that exploit regulatory gaps between existing frameworks.

sections.label: Mandatory imprisonment for import offences
sections.summary: The introduction of mandatory imprisonment for serious import and supply offences sends a strong deterrent signal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The introduction of mandatory imprisonment for serious import and supply offences sends a strong deterrent signal.

sections.label: Offence for allowing storage
sections.summary: Under new section 18A, an owner or occupier commits an offence if they allow storage of these prohibited items unless they exercised due care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under the new section 18A, an owner or occupier commits an offence if they allow the storage of these prohibited items unless they have exercised "due care".

sections.label: Review of Part 3A framework
sections.summary: Given rapid evolution of synthetic psychoactive substances, the Ministry is encouraged to consider a formal review of the Part 3A framework within three to five years of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Given the rapid evolution of synthetic psychoactive substances, I would encourage the Ministry to consider a formal review of the Part 3A framework within three to five years of implementation.

sections.label: Effective implementation of the Bill
sections.summary: Success depends on effective enforcement, rehabilitation and family support, so that enforcement and support structures stay one step ahead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Its success will depend on how effectively we implement enforcement, strengthen rehabilitation and support families as they navigate these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we implement this Bill effectively, we can ensure that our laws' enforcement and support structures remain one step ahead.

sections.label: Students caught vaping yearly
sections.summary: More than 3,000 students were caught vaping every year between 2022 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 3,000 students were caught vaping every year between 2022 and 2024.

sections.label: Etomidate temporary Class C classification
sections.summary: Since September 2025, etomidate and its analogues have been Class C controlled drugs under the Misuse of Drugs Act for six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since September 2025, etomidate and its analogues have been classified as Class C controlled drugs under the Misuse of Drugs Act, for a period of six months while we awaited this Bill.

sections.label: Stiffer vape trafficking punishments
sections.summary: New Parts 3 and 3A introduce amendments enacting stiffer punishments for trafficking and selling vapes laced with dangerous psychoactive substances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new Part 3 and 3A will introduce amendments to enact stiffer punishments for the trafficking and selling of vapes laced with dangerous psychoactive substances.

sections.label: National protocol for youth vaping addiction
sections.summary: The member proposes MOH assemble psychiatrists, addiction specialists and counsellors to create a national protocol guiding parents, teachers and schools supporting youths breaking vaping addiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The result may end up being an inconsistent and patchy response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to propose that MOH consider assembling a team of child and adolescent psychiatrists, qualified addiction specialists and professional counsellors, to come up with a national protocol or programme that will provide clear guidance to parents, teachers and schools as they support our youths who are trying to break the addiction of vaping.

sections.label: Etomidate temporary Class C measure
sections.summary: The Government moved fast and in September last year etomidate was classified as a Class C drug as a temporary measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government moved fast, and in September last year, etomidate was classified as a Class C drug as a temporary measure.

sections.label: Etomidate reclassification to specified psychoactive substance
sections.summary: The Bill provides for reclassifying etomidate from a Class C controlled drug under the MDA to a specified psychoactive substance under the proposed TVCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The current Bill provides for the reclassification of etomidate from a Class C controlled drug under the MDA to a "specified psychoactive substance" under the proposed TVCA.

sections.label: Minister empowered to amend Schedule
sections.summary: The Minister will be empowered to amend the Schedule by order in the Gazette, letting new psychoactive substances be added swiftly without full legislative amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister will be empowered to amend the Schedule by order in the Gazette, enabling new psychoactive substances to be added swiftly without the need for a full legislative amendment each time.

sections.label: Listing psychoactive substances under TVCA
sections.summary: Asks what considerations will determine whether a psychoactive substance is listed under the TVCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, in future, what considerations will determine whether a psychoactive substance is to be listed under the TVCA?

sections.label: HSA and CNB overlap
sections.summary: Asks how overlap between HSA and CNB rehabilitation powers will be resolved when both Acts potentially apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, where a case is potentially caught by both Acts, say, multiple substances were found, and the Chief Executive of the HSA and the Director of the CNB both have the power to order an offender to undergo rehabilitation under the relevant provisions of the two Acts, how will this overlap be resolved between the HSA and the CNB?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The provisions requiring responsible persons to act when prohibited products are used on their premises and the measures addressing exposure of children and young persons are important complements to criminal penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's firm stance against drug abuse has been an important pillar of our social stability and public safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We must not be seen to compromise on this when new substances emerge.

sections.label: Etomidate vaping quit cases
sections.summary: More than 110 persons came forward to quit etomidate vaping in the past six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the past six months, more than 110 persons came forward to quit etomidate vaping.

sections.label: Penalties for vaping offences
sections.summary: Vaping offenders face prosecution and fines up to $10,000; etomidate vapers are detained in the DRC for treatment and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For vaping, they will be prosecuted and subject to the increased fine, up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For etomidate vaping, they will be detained in the DRC for institutional treatment and rehabilitation.

sections.label: Penalties for SPS products
sections.summary: If products contain SPS, penalties will be as severe and aligned to Class C controlled drugs under the MDA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If the products contain SPS, the penalties will be as severe and aligned to those for Class C controlled drugs under the MDA.

sections.label: Online advertisements removed and websites blocked
sections.summary: Over 10,000 online advertisements were removed since 2024 and 27 websites blocked under the OCHA since September last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Over 10,000 online advertisements were removed since 2024 and 27 websites blocked under the OCHA since September last year.

sections.label: Vaporiser smuggling cases detected
sections.summary: HSA and ICA joint operations detected 59 large-scale smuggling cases in 2025, seizing around 230,000 vaporisers and related products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On vaporisers specifically, with the help of intelligence sharing, joint operations by HSA and ICA detected 59 large-scale smuggling cases in 2025, seizing around 230,000 vaporisers and related products.

sections.label: Due care handbook for owners
sections.summary: HSA will publish a handbook on due care for owners and occupiers under the new storage offence, with the Bill commencing 1 May.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: HSA will publish a handbook of best practices today on their website to illustrate what constitutes "due care" by owners and occupiers of land, buildings and places under the new offence of allowing other individuals to store prohibited products or their components in these spaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We intend for the Bill to commence on 1 May and will provide support to responsible persons and owners and occupiers before then.

sections.label: Authorised officers enforcement capacity
sections.summary: Enforcement is not done by HSA alone, with more than 13,000 officers authorised to-date.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, the enforcement is not done just by HSA alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This has multiplied our effective enforcement capacity, with more than 13,000 officers authorised to-date.

sections.label: Rehabilitation capacity review
sections.summary: After six months of operating rehabilitation programmes, sufficient capacity has been provided, including in the DRC, and will be regularly reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On rehabilitation capacity, having operated these programmes for the past six months, we have provided for sufficient capacity, including in the DRC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will regularly review capacity utilisation and projections, based on the latest offender numbers and trends and make the necessary adjustments.

sections.label: Listing substances in TVCA Schedule
sections.summary: New psychoactive substances in tobacco products, vaporisers or imitation tobacco products can be listed in the TVCA Schedule by Gazette order.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If another psychoactive substance or product emerges in tobacco products, vaporisers or imitation tobacco products, it can be listed in the Schedule of TVCA fairly quickly, by amending the Schedule via an order in the Gazette made by the Minister for Health.

sections.label: Nicotine emission yield cap
sections.summary: Singapore's nicotine emission yield has been capped at 1.0 milligrams since 2013 under the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Limits on Certain Substances) Regulations 2010.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is possible to do so under the new section 14.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I do hear the Member's suggesting that the UK has a cap of 1.0 milligram and actually in Singapore, our nicotine emission yield is also capped at 1.0 milligrams since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, if the Member were to look this up, it is actually under the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Limits on Certain Substances) Regulations 2010.
